cards.subject: A design token
says: stores one named design decision such as a colour, spacing or radius value
replaces a hard-coded value with a name that design and code both use
can be exported from one source to several platforms
cards.use: need one source of truth for a brand colour across web and mobile
not: is a security credential that signs users in

cards.subject: A primitive token
says: holds a raw value such as a hex colour or a pixel size
is named for what the value is, not where it is used
cards.use: define the full list of raw colours before deciding how they are used
not: is named for the component that consumes it

cards.subject: A semantic token
says: is named for its purpose, such as text-primary or surface-error
points at a primitive token
lets a theme change meaning-based values without editing components
cards.use: need the same text colour role to differ between light and dark themes
not: holds a raw hex value with no alias

cards.subject: A component token
says: scopes a value to a single component, such as button-background
usually aliases a semantic token
lets one component be restyled without affecting others
cards.use: need one component to differ slightly from the system default
not: replaces the need for semantic tokens entirely

cards.subject: Token aliasing
says: lets one token reference another instead of repeating its value
builds the layers from primitive to semantic to component
means a single edit upstream flows to every dependent token
cards.use: need a change to a base colour to reach every token built on it

cards.subject: A hard-coded value
says: is a literal colour or size written directly into a component
makes a rebrand require edits in many places
is the main cause of drift between design and code
cards.use: spot why a global colour change missed several screens
not: is the recommended way to store brand colours

cards.subject: A spacing scale
says: offers a fixed set of steps such as 4, 8, 16 and 24 pixels
replaces arbitrary one-off margins and paddings
makes spacing predictable across screens
cards.use: want gaps between elements to look consistent everywhere
not: lets each designer pick any value per screen

cards.subject: A CSS custom property
says: is declared with a double-dash name such as --space-4
is read with the var() function
can be overridden inside a subtree so themes cascade
cards.use: need to expose a token to CSS so a theme can override it
not: is compiled away at build time so it cannot change at runtime

cards.subject: A token naming convention
says: makes tokens predictable by following a pattern such as category, property, variant and state
lets people guess a token name without searching for it
cards.use: agree how colour tokens for hover states should be named
not: encodes the current raw value in the name of semantic tokens

cards.subject: Style Dictionary
says: transforms token source files into platform outputs such as CSS variables
applies per-platform transforms to units and colour formats
keeps one token source for several codebases
cards.use: need web and native apps to build from the same token file
not: draws components on a design canvas

cards.subject: The DTCG token format
says: is a draft format from the W3C Design Tokens Community Group
stores each token with a $value and a $type in JSON
aims to let tools exchange tokens without custom converters
cards.use: want token files that different design and build tools can read
not: is a CSS-only syntax for variables

cards.subject: A theme
says: is a set of token values applied together
changes the look of an interface without changing component code
can be switched at runtime by overriding custom properties
cards.use: need a high-contrast variant of a product
not: requires rewriting every component

cards.subject: A design system
says: is a shared set of tokens, components, patterns and guidelines
gives design and engineering a common language
is a product that needs owners and maintenance
cards.use: want several teams to build consistent interfaces without redrawing buttons
not: is a single Figma file of logos

cards.subject: A component variant
says: is a defined version of a component that differs along one property such as size or emphasis
keeps a family of similar versions in one component
cards.use: need a button in small, medium and large sizes
not: is a separate unrelated component

cards.subject: A component state
says: describes how a component looks at a moment, such as hover, focus, pressed or disabled
needs a design for each interactive moment, not only the default
cards.use: need to show a user that a control is currently unavailable
not: is a permanent size option chosen by the designer

cards.subject: A component prop
says: configures one instance of a component, such as size or disabled
forms the public API a consumer uses
cards.use: want a consumer to change a component's label without editing its code
not: lets a consumer rewrite the internals of a component

cards.subject: A slot
says: is a named place where a consumer supplies content
lets one component host different icons or text without extra options
cards.use: need a card whose header area can hold an icon, a badge or nothing
not: is a fixed value that cannot be replaced

cards.subject: Composition
says: builds complex UI by combining small components
avoids adding an option to one component for every new case
keeps each part simple to test
cards.use: find a way to avoid one card component with twenty options
not: means copying a component and editing the copy

cards.subject: Boolean prop explosion
says: adds a true-or-false flag for each new case
creates combinations that are impossible to test or document
is usually solved with variants or composition
cards.use: explain why a component with many flags became hard to maintain
not: keeps a component API small

cards.subject: Atomic design
says: organises UI into atoms, molecules, organisms, templates and pages
was described by Brad Frost
gives a shared vocabulary for building up from small parts
cards.use: need a way to name levels from a single input to a full page layout
not: is a method for reducing file size

cards.subject: A pattern
says: solves a recurring user problem by combining several components
describes when and how to use the combination, such as a search form
cards.use: document how a filter bar, chips and results list work together
not: is a single indivisible control

cards.subject: A headless component
says: provides behaviour and accessibility without any styling
lets each team apply its own visual design on top
handles keyboard and focus logic for the consumer
cards.use: need to reuse menu behaviour under a different visual brand
not: ships with fixed colours and spacing

cards.subject: A compound component
says: splits a component into cooperating parts that share implicit state
is seen in Tabs with a list, tab and panel
lets consumers arrange the parts freely
cards.use: want a tabs component where the consumer controls the markup order
not: is one flat component that takes a long props list

cards.subject: An escape hatch
says: lets a consumer override a component beyond its official API
trades some consistency for flexibility
should be tracked, because many uses signal a missing variant
cards.use: decide how to let a team style a component outside its options
not: improves consistency by allowing any override

cards.subject: A polymorphic component
says: renders as a different HTML element through a prop such as as
keeps the same styling while changing the underlying tag
needs care so semantics stay correct
cards.use: want a button style applied to a link without duplicating the component
not: always renders a div

cards.subject: A primary button
says: marks the single most important action in a view
has the strongest visual emphasis of the button set
cards.use: need to highlight the main call to action on a form
not: should appear many times in one view to give equal emphasis

cards.subject: A destructive button
says: is styled distinctly for an action that deletes or cannot be undone
is usually backed by a confirmation or an undo
cards.use: need to signal that clicking will remove data
not: is styled identically to every other button

cards.subject: A modal dialog
says: blocks interaction with the page behind it until dismissed
must move focus inside and return it on close
is overused when the task could happen inline
cards.use: need the user to confirm a decision before continuing
not: leaves the rest of the page fully usable

cards.subject: A toast
says: shows a brief non-blocking message that fades after a short time
suits low-importance confirmation
can be missed, so it should not carry critical information
cards.use: want to confirm that a draft was saved without interrupting the user
not: blocks the page until dismissed

cards.subject: An inline alert
says: stays visible next to the content it concerns
persists until the issue is fixed or dismissed
cards.use: need to show a form-level problem that must not disappear on its own
not: disappears automatically after a few seconds

cards.subject: A tabbed interface
says: switches between related panels shown one at a time in the same space
keeps peer sections of equal importance side by side in a tab list
cards.use: need to show profile, billing and security settings in one place
not: stack every section open at the same time

cards.subject: An accordion
says: expands and collapses sections under headings
lets users scan headings before opening detail
cards.use: want a long FAQ that can be scanned by question
not: shows exactly one panel and hides all other headings

cards.subject: A skeleton screen
says: shows grey placeholder shapes laid out like the coming content
reduces the sense of waiting and layout shift
cards.use: want to show page structure while data loads
not: is a final error page

cards.subject: An empty state
says: explains why nothing is shown
offers a clear next step, such as creating the first item
cards.use: design what a new user sees on a list with no items
not: shows only a blank area with no message

cards.subject: A radio button group
says: presents a few mutually exclusive options all visible at once
allows exactly one choice in the group
cards.use: need the user to choose one of three shipping speeds
not: allow any number of options to be selected

cards.subject: A checkbox group
says: allows zero or more independent choices
lets each box be toggled without affecting the others
cards.use: want a user to tick several notification types
not: allow only one choice from a group

cards.subject: A select menu
says: hides a longer list of mutually exclusive options until opened
saves space when there are too many options to show
cards.use: need a country field with many options
not: shows every option at all times

cards.subject: A toggle switch
says: applies a setting immediately as it is flipped
represents an on or off state
cards.use: want a setting that takes effect without a save button
not: is submitted later with the rest of a form

cards.subject: A form label
says: names a field in visible text that stays on screen
is linked to its input so clicking it focuses the field
gives the field its accessible name
cards.use: need every input to be understandable to a screen reader
not: can be replaced by placeholder text alone

cards.subject: A placeholder
says: shows example text inside an empty field
disappears when the user types
is not a substitute for a label
cards.use: want to hint at the format, such as a sample date
not: is announced as the permanent label by every assistive technology

cards.subject: Helper text
says: stays near a field to explain what is expected
is read to users when tied to the input
cards.use: need to state a password rule before the user types
not: appears only after an error occurs

cards.subject: A validation message
says: tells the user what went wrong and how to fix it
appears next to the field in error
is linked to the field so assistive technology announces it
cards.use: want a failed field to explain the problem in words
not: only changes the field border colour

cards.subject: A layout grid
says: divides a page into columns with consistent gutters and margins
helps align elements and creates rhythm
cards.use: need elements across pages to line up
not: fixes the exact pixel position of every element

cards.subject: A column grid
says: is often twelve columns because twelve divides evenly by 2, 3, 4 and 6
lets content span a chosen number of columns
cards.use: need a flexible layout that supports halves, thirds and quarters
not: must always have exactly 24 columns

cards.subject: A gutter
says: is the space between columns
keeps adjacent content from touching
cards.use: need breathing room between two cards in a row
not: is the space around the outside of the page

cards.subject: A breakpoint
says: is a viewport width at which the layout changes
is usually chosen where the content starts to break, not for particular devices
cards.use: decide when a sidebar should drop below the content
not: is a debugging pause in code

cards.subject: Mobile-first design
says: starts from the smallest layout and adds complexity at wider sizes
uses min-width media queries
forces a priority order for content
cards.use: want a layout where small screens get the simplest rules
not: designs for large screens first and removes things later

cards.subject: A container query
says: styles a component based on the size of its container rather than the viewport
lets a component adapt wherever it is placed
cards.use: need a card to rearrange itself in a narrow sidebar and a wide main area
not: responds only to the window width

cards.subject: CSS Grid
says: lays out content in rows and columns at the same time
suits whole-page and two-dimensional layouts
cards.use: need to place items in both rows and columns
not: lays out items in one dimension only

cards.subject: Flexbox
says: lays out items along one axis at a time
distributes space and alignment among items in a row or column
cards.use: need a toolbar of items that share space in a row
not: is built for two-dimensional page grids

cards.subject: A baseline grid
says: aligns lines of text to a repeating vertical rhythm
keeps text across columns sitting on common lines
cards.use: want text in neighbouring columns to line up
not: divides the page into horizontal columns

cards.subject: Whitespace
says: is empty space that separates and groups content
improves readability and focus
is part of the design, not wasted room
cards.use: want users to find the main message on a crowded page
not: is a defect to be filled with content

cards.subject: A type scale
says: defines a limited set of font sizes for the interface
keeps text hierarchy consistent
cards.use: choose the sizes for headings, body and captions
not: lets each page pick any size

cards.subject: A modular scale
says: grows sizes by a constant ratio such as 1.25
produces sizes that relate to one another
cards.use: generate heading sizes from a body size using a ratio
not: uses random increments

cards.subject: Line height
says: sets the vertical distance between lines of text
is commonly around 1.4 to 1.6 times the font size for body text
cards.use: fix text that feels cramped in a paragraph
not: sets the width of each line

cards.subject: Line length
says: is the number of characters on one line
is commonly kept near 45 to 75 characters for body text
cards.use: stop long paragraphs from being tiring to read
not: is controlled by line height

cards.subject: Letter spacing
says: adjusts the space between all characters in a run of text
is often loosened for small uppercase labels
cards.use: make small all-caps labels easier to read
not: adjusts the space between lines

cards.subject: A font stack
says: lists fallback fonts in order
ends with a generic family such as sans-serif
cards.use: keep text readable if the brand font fails to load
not: loads every listed font at once

cards.subject: A variable font
says: holds a range of weights or widths in one file
allows smooth values along an axis such as weight
cards.use: want many weights without many font files
not: contains only one fixed weight

cards.subject: Fluid typography
says: scales text smoothly between a minimum and maximum size
is often written with the CSS clamp function
cards.use: avoid abrupt size jumps between breakpoints
not: uses only fixed sizes per breakpoint

cards.subject: Font weight
says: varies stroke thickness from light to bold
signals emphasis without changing the size
cards.use: emphasise a key phrase inside body text
not: changes the typeface family

cards.subject: font-display swap
says: shows fallback text immediately while a web font loads
swaps in the web font when it arrives
can cause a visible shift when the fonts differ in size
cards.use: avoid invisible text during font load
not: hides all text until the font is ready

cards.subject: A colour palette
says: is the defined set of colours a system uses
includes neutrals, brand colours and status colours
cards.use: decide the colours for a product's interface
not: is limited to one brand colour

cards.subject: A tonal scale
says: lists lighter to darker steps of one hue, such as 50 to 900
gives predictable options for backgrounds, borders and text
cards.use: need several shades of one brand colour for different uses
not: lists unrelated colours

cards.subject: Contrast ratio
says: compares the luminance of two colours as a number
ranges from 1:1 for identical colours to 21:1 for black on white
cards.use: measure whether text stands out from its background
not: measures how colourful a colour is

cards.subject: A colour role
says: assigns meaning such as success, warning or error to a colour
must be reinforced by text or icons
cards.use: define which colour means danger across the product
not: uses colour as the only signal

cards.subject: Dark mode
says: uses a dark surface palette with adjusted token values
needs contrast re-checked rather than a simple inversion
often lowers saturation on bright colours
cards.use: offer a theme for low-light use
not: is a pure colour inversion of the light theme

cards.subject: The OKLCH colour space
says: models colour with lightness, chroma and hue
gives steps that look perceptually even
makes it easier to build palettes with matching lightness
cards.use: want tonal steps that look equally spaced
not: is limited to the old sRGB gamut

cards.subject: Colour-blind safe design
says: never relies on colour alone to convey meaning
adds icons, labels or patterns beside colour
cards.use: make a chart readable for people who cannot tell red from green
not: uses only red and green to differentiate states

cards.subject: WCAG
says: is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines published by the W3C
sets testable success criteria at levels A, AA and AAA
cards.use: need a recognised standard for web accessibility
not: is a design file format

cards.subject: POUR
says: names the four WCAG principles: perceivable, operable, understandable and robust
gives a frame for sorting accessibility issues
cards.use: remember the principles that organise the guidelines
not: is a list of four colours

cards.subject: Normal text contrast at AA
says: requires a ratio of at least 4.5:1
applies to text below the large-text size
cards.use: check ordinary body text against its background
not: requires 3:1

cards.subject: Large text contrast at AA
says: requires a ratio of at least 3:1
applies to text of 18 point or larger, or 14 point bold or larger
cards.use: check a big heading against its background
not: requires 7:1

cards.subject: Text contrast at AAA
says: requires 7:1 for normal text
requires 4.5:1 for large text
cards.use: meet the enhanced contrast level
not: requires 4.5:1 for normal text

cards.subject: Non-text contrast
says: requires at least 3:1 for interface component boundaries and meaningful graphics
covers things such as input borders and focus indicators
cards.use: check that a field border is visible enough
not: applies only to body text

cards.subject: Minimum target size
says: is 24 by 24 CSS pixels at WCAG 2.2 level AA
helps users with limited dexterity
cards.use: check that small icon buttons are easy to press
not: is 44 by 44 pixels at level A

cards.subject: Focus visible
says: requires a visible indicator on the element with keyboard focus
helps keyboard users know where they are
cards.use: make sure a tabbing user can see which control is active
not: lets a design remove the outline with no replacement

cards.subject: Semantic HTML
says: uses elements for their meaning, such as button, nav and heading
gives roles and behaviour to assistive technology for free
cards.use: avoid rebuilding a button from a div
not: relies on ARIA to supply meaning where native elements exist

cards.subject: ARIA
says: adds roles and properties for assistive technology
fills gaps that native HTML cannot
changes semantics but adds no behaviour or styling
cards.use: describe a custom widget to a screen reader
not: makes a div keyboard operable by itself

cards.subject: An accessible name
says: is the text a screen reader announces for a control
comes from a label, visible text or aria-label
cards.use: fix an icon-only button that screen readers announce as just button
not: is always taken from the placeholder

cards.subject: Alternative text
says: gives a text equivalent for an image
is left empty for purely decorative images
cards.use: describe a chart image for people who cannot see it
not: should always begin with image of

cards.subject: A focus trap
says: keeps keyboard focus inside a modal dialog while it is open
lets users escape with the Escape key and returns focus on close
cards.use: stop tabbing from moving to the page behind a dialog
not: is a bug that should be avoided in every dialog

cards.subject: Reduced motion
says: is a user preference that asks for less animation
is read with the prefers-reduced-motion media query
cards.use: respect users who feel sick from movement
not: is an option that only works on mobile

cards.subject: Reflow
says: requires content to be usable at 320 CSS pixels wide without two-dimensional scrolling
is tested by zooming to 400 percent
cards.use: check a page works for people who zoom in heavily
not: allows horizontal scrolling for body text

cards.subject: A skip link
says: lets keyboard users jump past repeated navigation
is often the first focusable element on a page
cards.use: avoid forcing keyboard users through twenty menu links on every page
not: hides content from screen readers

cards.subject: A live region
says: announces content changes to screen readers without moving focus
suits status updates such as saved or error messages
cards.use: announce a form submission result without moving focus
not: moves keyboard focus to the new content

cards.subject: Semantic versioning
says: numbers releases as major, minor and patch
raises the major number for breaking changes
raises the minor number for backward-compatible additions
cards.use: communicate that a release will break existing usage
not: raises the patch number for every new feature

cards.subject: A changelog
says: records what changed in each release
helps consumers decide whether and how to upgrade
cards.use: tell teams what is different in version 3
not: lists future plans only

cards.subject: A deprecation policy
says: announces that a component will be removed, with a notice period
points consumers to the replacement
avoids surprise breaking changes
cards.use: retire an old button without breaking teams
not: removes the component the same day it is announced

cards.subject: A breaking change
says: requires consumers to change their code or designs to upgrade
belongs in a major release
cards.use: decide how to ship a renamed prop
not: can safely ship in a patch release

cards.subject: A contribution model
says: describes how teams propose and add to the system
comes in centralised, federated or hybrid forms
cards.use: decide whether product teams can add components
not: is the same as a licence

cards.subject: An RFC process
says: collects a written proposal and feedback before a change is made
creates a record of why a decision was taken
cards.use: agree a major change to the component API with many teams
not: lets one person decide privately

cards.subject: Design drift
says: is the gradual divergence of products from the system
grows when teams copy and tweak components
cards.use: explain why screens no longer match the library
not: is a feature of tokens

cards.subject: An adoption metric
says: measures how much of a product uses system components
helps prioritise the work with most impact
cards.use: show whether teams actually use the system
not: measure how many designers work on the team

cards.subject: A release channel
says: separates stable releases from beta or canary ones
lets teams test changes before they become the default
cards.use: let teams try new tokens before the major release
not: ships every change to everyone at once

cards.subject: A usage guideline
says: explains when and how to use a component
includes do and do-not examples
cards.use: help a designer decide between a modal and an inline alert
not: only list a component's colour values

cards.subject: Anatomy documentation
says: labels the parts of a component such as icon, label and container
gives teams a shared vocabulary for the pieces
cards.use: name every part of a card so teams discuss it the same way
not: lists the version history

cards.subject: A do and do-not example
says: shows correct use beside a common mistake
makes a rule easier to apply than text alone
cards.use: teach a rule with a good and a bad image
not: replace the accessibility notes

cards.subject: An accessibility note
says: records keyboard behaviour, roles and contrast for a component
lets consumers build on tested behaviour
cards.use: tell developers how a dialog handles focus
not: describes only the component colours

cards.subject: A living style guide
says: is documentation generated from or tied to real components
stays accurate because it updates with the code
cards.use: avoid docs that go stale after a release
not: is a static PDF that is updated yearly

cards.subject: A content style guide
says: sets voice, tone and writing rules for interface text
keeps button labels and messages consistent
cards.use: decide whether to say Sign in or Log in everywhere
not: covers only colour choices

cards.subject: A single source of truth
says: keeps one authoritative place for design decisions
prevents conflicting copies in different tools
cards.use: stop two files showing different button colours
not: spreads decisions across many documents

cards.subject: An iconography guideline
says: sets the grid, stroke and style of icons
keeps icon meaning consistent
cards.use: make new icons match the existing set
not: lets each designer pick any style

cards.subject: A design handoff
says: passes a finished design to developers with the detail needed to build it
includes specs, assets and behaviour notes
cards.use: make sure engineers can build a screen without guessing
not: ends the designer's involvement

cards.subject: A design spec
says: states sizes, spacing, colours and typography for a design
references tokens instead of raw values where possible
cards.use: tell a developer the exact padding of a card
not: describes only the final colours of the logo

cards.subject: A redline
says: marks measurements and spacing directly on a design
is partly replaced by inspect tools in design software
cards.use: annotate gaps between elements on a mockup
not: is a user research method

cards.subject: Auto layout
says: makes a frame resize and reflow its contents
mirrors how flexbox arranges items in code
cards.use: build a design that behaves like the coded layout
not: fixes every item at an absolute position

cards.subject: Design and code parity
says: means the design library and the code library use the same names and structure
reduces translation errors
cards.use: keep Button in the design file the same as Button in code
not: means designers must write production code

cards.subject: Storybook
says: lets developers build and view components in isolation
documents each state of a component
cards.use: review all states of a button without running the app
not: is a design tool for drawing mock-ups

cards.subject: Visual regression testing
says: compares screenshots before and after a change
flags unintended visual differences
cards.use: catch a style change that moved a button
not: checks that code compiles

cards.subject: An interaction spec
says: describes behaviour such as transitions, timing and what happens on error
covers what static mockups cannot show
cards.use: explain how a menu opens and closes
not: lists static colours only

cards.subject: Definition of done for design
says: states what must be true before a design is considered shippable
includes accessibility and all states
cards.use: agree when a component is ready for release
not: is satisfied once the mockup looks nice

cards.subject: User experience
says: covers a person's whole interaction with a product
includes usability, usefulness and emotion
cards.use: describe more than how a screen looks
not: refers only to visual style

cards.subject: Usability
says: is how effectively and easily users reach their goals
is measured by success, speed, errors and satisfaction
cards.use: judge whether people can finish a task
not: describes only how attractive an interface is

cards.subject: Visibility of system status
says: keeps users informed through timely feedback about what is happening
is the Nielsen heuristic that a progress bar satisfies
cards.use: show progress while an upload runs
not: tells users to read the manual

cards.subject: Match between system and the real world
says: uses words and concepts familiar to the user rather than system terms
is the Nielsen heuristic violated by internal jargon
cards.use: replace internal jargon with the user's own words
not: encourages use of technical terms

cards.subject: User control and freedom
says: gives users a clearly marked way out, such as undo and cancel
is the Nielsen heuristic violated by a flow with no exit
cards.use: let a user back out of an action by mistake
not: locks users into each step

cards.subject: Error prevention
says: stops problems before they occur, for example with constraints and confirmation
is the Nielsen heuristic that disabling an impossible option satisfies
cards.use: stop users from entering an invalid date
not: shows a helpful message after the error occurs

cards.subject: Recognition rather than recall
says: keeps options visible so users need not remember them
is the Nielsen heuristic that suggests recent items satisfy
cards.use: show recent searches rather than expecting users to remember
not: rewards users who memorise commands

cards.subject: Visual hierarchy
says: guides attention using size, contrast, colour and position
shows what is most important first
cards.use: make the main action stand out on a page
not: gives every element equal weight

cards.subject: An affordance
says: is a property that suggests how something can be used
helps a control look interactive
cards.use: make a button look pressable
not: is a hidden feature unrelated to the visual design

cards.subject: A signifier
says: is a perceivable cue that shows where an action is possible
was named by Don Norman to clarify affordances
cards.use: add a visible cue showing a card can be dragged
not: is a hidden capability of an object

cards.subject: Feedback
says: tells the user that the system received an action and what happened
can be visual, textual or haptic
cards.use: confirm a button press registered
not: hides the result until the next page

cards.subject: Fitts's law
says: predicts that time to reach a target depends on its distance and size
favours large targets placed near the pointer
cards.use: decide how big a frequent button should be
not: says users scan pages in an F pattern

cards.subject: Hick's law
says: says decision time grows with the number and complexity of choices
supports reducing and grouping options
cards.use: simplify a menu with thirty choices
not: predicts the time to reach a target

cards.subject: Jakob's law
says: says users spend most of their time on other sites, so they prefer familiar patterns
supports using conventions
cards.use: decide whether to move the cart icon to an unusual place
not: says to reinvent navigation to stand out

cards.subject: Progressive disclosure
says: shows only the most needed options first
reveals advanced options on request
cards.use: hide advanced settings until a user asks
not: shows every option on the first screen

cards.subject: The Gestalt law of proximity
says: says elements placed close together are seen as related
helps group a label with its field
cards.use: group related form fields without drawing boxes
not: says similar colours always mean the same group

cards.subject: A mental model
says: is a person's belief about how a system works
causes confusion when an interface contradicts it
cards.use: explain why a user expected a trash icon to delete
not: is the design team's internal model of the code

cards.subject: A usability test
says: watches real users attempt tasks with a product
uncovers problems that opinions miss
cards.use: find out why users abandon the checkout
not: asks users what they prefer without any tasks

cards.subject: Think-aloud
says: asks participants to say their thoughts as they work
reveals confusion and expectations in the moment
cards.use: understand what a user expects while using a prototype
not: interrupts users with questions after each click

cards.subject: Card sorting
says: asks participants to group topics into categories
informs navigation and information architecture
cards.use: design menu labels and groups
not: tests whether people can find items in an existing menu

cards.subject: Tree testing
says: checks whether users can find items in a text-only hierarchy
evaluates the structure without visual design
cards.use: validate a new navigation structure before design
not: asks users to create new categories

cards.subject: A heuristic evaluation
says: has experts review an interface against usability principles
finds issues without recruiting users
cards.use: get quick expert feedback before testing
not: relies on random users clicking

cards.subject: A survey
says: collects answers from many people at low cost
tells you what people say, not what they do
cards.use: gather opinions from a large audience
not: watches users complete tasks

cards.subject: The System Usability Scale
says: is a ten-item questionnaire
produces a single score from 0 to 100
cards.use: compare perceived usability across releases
not: is a measure of page load speed

cards.subject: An A/B test
says: compares two versions with different users at the same time
needs enough traffic to reach a reliable conclusion
cards.use: decide which of two button labels gets more clicks
not: shows the same version to everyone

cards.subject: Contextual inquiry
says: observes people in their real environment while they work
uncovers workarounds and constraints that interviews miss
cards.use: learn how nurses use a system during a shift
not: uses a lab with scripted tasks only

cards.subject: The Brand System guideline document
says: runs to 30 to 60 pages in the Guru Graphics Brand System engagement
gathers the logo, colour, typography and voice rules in one document
cards.use: explain what the largest Guru Graphics engagement hands over
not: is a website build

The Brand System campaign style rule

cards.subject: The Brand System accessibility standard
says: is included in the Guru Graphics Brand System
sets the contrast and accessibility rules the brand must follow
cards.use: explain how Guru Graphics covers accessible brand design
not: is offered only as a separate add-on

cards.subject: The Brand System colour and typography rule
says: belongs to the Guru Graphics Brand System guidelines
says which colours and typefaces the brand uses and how
cards.use: explain where a client finds approved fonts and colours

cards.subject: The Brand System voice rule
says: covers brand voice and writing tone in the Guru Graphics Brand System
guides how words sound across channels
cards.use: explain where tone of writing is defined for a client brand
not: is covered by logo rules

The Brand System campaign style rule

says: defines campaign and advertising style in the Guru Graphics Brand System
extends the identity into promotion
cards.use: explain how a brand should look in adverts
not: is covered by accessibility standards

says: covers design and branding only

qa.q: What is the main purpose of a design system?
qa.right: To give teams a shared, reusable set of components and guidelines for consistent interfaces
wrong: To replace the need for user research
To store the final copy of every project file
To limit a product to one screen size
qa.why: A design system gives design and engineering a common library and rules.

qa.q: What is a design token?
qa.right: A named value for a design decision such as a colour or spacing step
wrong: A single-use password for a design tool
A screenshot of a finished page
qa.why: Tokens replace raw values with names shared by design and code.

qa.q: Which text contrast ratio does WCAG AA require for normal body text?
qa.right: At least 4.5:1
qa.why: AA is 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

qa.q: Which is the best element for a control that triggers an action?
qa.right: A native button element
wrong: A div with a click handler
A span styled to look like a button
qa.why: A native button brings keyboard support and semantics for free.

qa.q: What does a primary button signal?
qa.right: The most important action in the view
wrong: That the action cannot be undone
qa.why: Only one primary action per view keeps emphasis meaningful.

qa.q: What is alt text for a meaningful image?
qa.right: A text equivalent for people who cannot see the image
wrong: A caption shown under every image
A title that appears in the page tab
A way to make the file smaller
qa.why: Alt text is the accessible text alternative.

qa.q: What does a layout grid help with?
qa.right: Aligning elements and keeping consistent spacing across pages
qa.why: Grids create consistent columns, gutters and margins.

qa.q: A team hard-codes #1A73E8 in forty components. The brand colour changes. What is the best long-term fix?
qa.right: Replace the literals with a semantic colour token that aliases a primitive
wrong: Search and replace the hex value each time it changes
Ask designers to avoid changing the brand colour
Keep both colours and let each team choose
qa.why: A token layer lets one change flow everywhere.

qa.q: Which naming is more useful for a semantic token?
qa.right: color-text-primary
qa.why: Semantic names state purpose so the value can change without renaming.

qa.q: A form shows a field with only a placeholder as its label. What is the main problem?
qa.right: The label disappears when typing and is unreliable as an accessible name
wrong: Screen readers always announce placeholders twice
qa.why: Use a visible label linked to the input.

qa.q: A user sees a green tick next to a saved file and a red cross next to an error, with no text. Who is most likely to miss the meaning?
qa.right: A person who cannot distinguish red from green
wrong: A person who prefers dark mode
A person using a wide monitor
A person on a fast connection
qa.why: Colour must be backed by shape or text.

qa.q: What do tabs do compared with an accordion?
qa.right: Show one panel at a time among peers in the same space
wrong: Always open every section at once
Load a new page for each panel
qa.why: Tabs swap content in place; accordions expand sections under headings.

qa.q: A designer wants a card layout that rearranges at wider widths. Which unit of change is this?
qa.right: A breakpoint
qa.why: A breakpoint is where the layout changes.

qa.q: Why is body text commonly kept to roughly 45 to 75 characters per line?
qa.right: Lines that are too long or too short tire the reader
wrong: It satisfies a WCAG level A rule
qa.why: Line length affects readability.

qa.q: A pointer user cannot tell which button is hovered or pressed. What is missing?
qa.right: Designed interactive states
qa.why: Components need hover, pressed, focus and disabled states.

qa.q: Which is the best way to give a screen reader a name for an icon-only button?
qa.right: Add an accessible name such as aria-label
wrong: Add a tooltip that only shows on hover
qa.why: The accessible name comes from a label or aria-label.

qa.q: A design file labels a button Primary but the code calls it Main. What is the likely consequence?
qa.right: Translation errors and drift between design and code
qa.why: Parity of names reduces confusion.

qa.q: A team renames a component prop from size to scale. Which release should this ship in?
qa.right: A major release with a migration note
qa.why: Renaming a prop breaks consumers, so semantic versioning requires a major release.

qa.q: A design system team wants to remove an old component. What should they do first?
qa.right: Announce deprecation with a timeline and a replacement
wrong: Hide it from the docs only
qa.why: A deprecation policy avoids surprise breakage.

qa.q: A product team needs a button variant that the system does not have. What process fits a federated model?
qa.right: Propose it through the contribution process and review it
wrong: Copy the button into the product and change it
Wait indefinitely for the core team
Use an inline style on every instance
qa.why: Contribution models keep additions consistent.

qa.q: A modal dialog opens, but a keyboard user can tab to links behind it. What is the fix?
qa.right: Trap focus inside the dialog and return it on close
qa.why: Focus must stay in the dialog while it is open.

qa.q: A user presses Tab and cannot see where focus is. Which WCAG idea is broken?
qa.right: Focus visible
qa.why: Keyboard users need a visible focus indicator.

qa.q: Which statement about the toast pattern is correct?
qa.right: It suits low-importance confirmations because it can be missed
wrong: It is the best way to show critical errors
It blocks the page until dismissed
qa.why: Critical information should persist in context, not fade away.

qa.q: A product page loads data slowly and the layout jumps when it arrives. What helps?
qa.right: A skeleton screen that reserves the layout
qa.why: Placeholders keep layout stable.

qa.q: A list page has no items for a new user. What should the empty state include?
qa.right: An explanation and a clear next step
wrong: A random illustration with no text
qa.why: Empty states should guide the user.

qa.q: Which is the better CSS for a token that a dark theme can override?
qa.right: Declare a custom property and read it with var()
wrong: Write the hex value in every rule
Use an image for the colour
Inline the colour in HTML attributes
qa.why: Custom properties cascade and can be overridden per theme.

qa.q: What does this CSS do?
qa.right: Applies a style only when the user asks for reduced motion
qa.why: The media query reads the user's operating system preference.

qa.q: Which tells a mobile browser to match layout width to the device?
qa.right: The viewport meta tag with width=device-width
wrong: A meta tag that disables zoom
A link to a mobile stylesheet
A heading with a data-mobile attribute
qa.why: The viewport tag controls the layout viewport.

qa.q: A checkout form shows a red border only when a field is invalid. What is missing?
qa.right: A text message tied to the field that says what is wrong
qa.why: Errors must not rely on colour alone and need text.

qa.q: A product designer asks if a setting should be a toggle or a checkbox plus Save button. The setting changes immediately. Which fits?
qa.right: A toggle switch
qa.why: Toggles apply immediately.

qa.q: A team asks for a Card component with 18 boolean props. What is the best response?
qa.right: Introduce variants and composition to avoid combinations that cannot be tested
wrong: Add the props, the API will be fine
Ship two Card components with no documentation
Hide the props from the docs
qa.why: Boolean prop explosion is solved with variants and slots.

qa.q: Which pair of colours meets AA for normal text?
qa.right: Colours measured at 4.6:1
qa.why: 4.5:1 is the AA minimum.

qa.q: Large text of 24 px regular needs which minimum ratio at AA?
qa.why: Large text, 18 pt or 24 px, needs 3:1 at AA.

qa.q: An input border measures 2:1 against its background. What does WCAG non-text contrast say?
qa.right: It fails because component boundaries need at least 3:1
wrong: It passes because borders are decorative
qa.why: Interface components need 3:1.

qa.q: Small icon buttons are 16 by 16 CSS pixels with no spacing. Which WCAG 2.2 AA criterion is at risk?
qa.right: Target size minimum
qa.why: The 2.2 minimum is 24 by 24 CSS pixels (with spacing exceptions).

qa.q: A design token JSON file has this structure. What is $type?
qa.right: The kind of value, such as colour or dimension
wrong: The CSS selector for the token
qa.why: The DTCG format stores a value and a type for each token.

qa.q: A team wants web and native apps to share colours from one file. What tool category fits?
qa.right: A token transformer such as Style Dictionary
qa.why: Token tools output many platform formats from one source.

qa.q: A team ships a new component with a bug. A visual regression suite catches it. How?
qa.right: By comparing screenshots before and after the change
qa.why: Visual regression compares rendered output.

qa.q: A test with five users found a navigation problem. What is the best next step?
qa.right: Fix it and test again with new participants
wrong: Ignore it because five is too few
qa.why: Small rounds of testing are cheap and iterative.

qa.q: You want to know if people can find a page in a proposed menu with no visual design. Which method?
qa.right: Tree testing
qa.why: Tree testing checks findability in a text hierarchy.

qa.q: You need to discover how people group topics before building navigation. Which method?
qa.right: Card sorting
qa.why: Card sorting reveals mental groupings.

qa.q: Which Nielsen heuristic does a progress bar during upload support?
qa.right: Visibility of system status
qa.why: Progress feedback keeps users informed.

qa.q: A form disables the Submit button until required fields are valid. Which heuristic does this mainly serve?
qa.right: Error prevention
qa.why: It prevents invalid submission.

qa.q: A settings page lists 40 options at once and users freeze. Which law explains this?
qa.right: Hick's law
qa.why: Decision time grows with the number of choices.

qa.q: A frequently used button is tiny and in a corner. Which law suggests a problem?
qa.right: Fitts's law
qa.why: Targets should be large and close.

qa.q: A team uses an as prop to render the same button style as an anchor. What risk must they manage?
qa.right: Keeping the correct semantics for the rendered element
qa.why: A polymorphic component must preserve correct roles and behaviour.

qa.q: A dark theme was made by inverting every light colour. What is the likely issue?
qa.right: Contrast and saturation can fail, so values need re-checking
qa.why: Dark themes need their own token values.

qa.q: Many teams use an escape hatch to override a component. What does that signal?
qa.right: A missing variant or API gap worth addressing
qa.why: Frequent overrides indicate the system lacks something.

qa.q: A page works at 1280 px but needs horizontal scrolling at 320 px for text. Which criterion fails?
qa.right: Reflow
qa.why: Content must reflow at 320 CSS px without two-dimensional scrolling.

qa.q: A status message must be announced to screen readers without moving focus. Which technique?
qa.right: A live region such as role=status
qa.why: Live regions announce changes.

qa.q: A design system has strong docs but low adoption. What should the team check first?
qa.right: Whether the components solve the product teams' real needs and are easy to adopt
qa.why: Adoption depends on fit and ease of use, not documentation alone.

qa.q: A product team shows a modal for every confirmation, and users dismiss without reading. What is a better approach?
qa.right: Use the lightest pattern that fits, such as inline confirmation or undo
qa.why: Overusing modals trains users to ignore them.

qa.q: A researcher interviews users in a meeting room about their workflow. Why might contextual inquiry add value?
qa.right: It shows workarounds and constraints visible only in the real environment
wrong: It removes the need for analysis
qa.why: Observation in context reveals what interviews miss.

qa.q: Guru Graphics describes its Brand System guidelines. Which content is stated for them?
qa.right: 30 to 60 pages with logo, colour and typography rules and accessibility and contrast standards
qa.why: The sources list these deliverables in the Brand System engagement.

qa.q: A client asks Guru Graphics to build their website and mobile app. What does the source say about the studio's scope?
qa.right: The studio does design and branding only, not websites or software
wrong: It builds websites for all clients
qa.why: The sources state design and branding only.

qa.q: Which is typical for a Guru Graphics Brand System engagement?
qa.right: About 8 to 12 weeks
qa.why: The sources give a typical 8-12 weeks.
